name: Reconciliation
summary: Reconciles payments, bank and payouts: reads bank lines and processor payouts, matches each payout to its deposit and each receipt to its invoice, notes the matches, and queues every payment for approval. Crons read and draft; a person approves every ledger write.

processor-payouts.evidence: 8 calls describe pulling the bank feed and recording processor payouts by hand, mostly in Xero

covered_by.match-customer-receipts: match (payouts to deposits, receipts to invoices, payment queued for approval)
covered_by.record-keeping: match (internal note on the bank line)

unclear.evidence: 11 calls describe supplier payment matching and record keeping done by hand in Xero

covered_by.record-keeping: match (internal note on the bank line)

crons.name: pull
crons.summary: Bank lines from each Xero bank account and payouts from Stripe, read into the store.

crons.name: match
crons.summary: Match payouts and receipts, note matches in Xero, queue payments for approval, write the worklist (22:30 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads, and an internal note on a bank line. A payment that applies money to an invoice is a live operation and waits for a person.

xero.covers: bank lines, invoice lookup, internal note, payment applied to an authorised invoice

stripe.covers: payouts (net amount to the bank) from balance transactions

gaps: MYOB: bank statements, customer and supplier payments are mapped as operations, but no adapter is built: its field names are only in HTML help pages, not a machine-readable spec.
Supplier payments (match-supplier-payments): matching bills to bank debits and batch payments needs a bills search operation this build does not map yet. Stays with the bookkeeper.
Fees and adjustments: splitting a Stripe payout into gross sales, fees and net deposit needs the owner's clearing account and chart of accounts. Not posted; the payout is matched to its deposit only.
Transfers between owner accounts and the accountant hand-off have no adapter here. The workflow lists them as manual steps.
Reviewer sign-off is the approval queue itself: a payment runs only when a person approves it in the CRM shell.
Stripe pagination reads up to 2,000 balance transactions a run. A business with more payouts in the lookback needs a larger window.
Both adapters are docs-only until a sandbox (a Xero demo company and a Stripe test account) proves the field names and the matching rules on real data.

evidence.calls: 40 of 52 reconciliation calls read; 19 describe the process; Xero is the most named tool (9 mentions, 7 of them in the record-keeping step)
evidence.platforms: Xero, Stripe and MYOB help and API pages mapped step by step: Xero supports bank feeds and partly receipts, MYOB supports bank feeds and receipts, Stripe supports payouts only partly
